story: As a security admin I want all privileged account passwords, keys and A2A credentials held in a vault and rotated on policy so that no static shared privileged secret persists outside managed control.
acceptance_criteria: 100% of in-scope privileged accounts onboarded to the vault; passwords/keys rotated on schedule and on check-in/release; no plaintext privileged credentials in scripts or config.

story: As a security admin I want privileged sessions brokered through an isolation proxy so that target credentials are never exposed to the operator endpoint and lateral movement is contained.
acceptance_criteria: Privileged sessions to in-scope targets route through the proxy with credential injection; no direct admin connections bypass the proxy; endpoint never receives the target secret.

story: As an auditor I want privileged sessions recorded with keystroke/command metadata so that every privileged action is attributable and forensically reviewable.
acceptance_criteria: Sessions to in-scope targets recorded with searchable metadata; recordings tamper-evident and retained per policy; high-risk commands flagged for review.

story: As a security architect I want privileged access granted just-in-time and time-bound so that no account carries always-on standing privilege between tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Standing privileged role memberships reduced to break-glass only; access granted JIT with expiry and approval; ZSP coverage tracked across in-scope targets.

story: As a security admin I want continuous discovery of privileged and local-admin accounts across the estate so that no privileged account escapes governance.
acceptance_criteria: Recurring discovery across AD, Unix, cloud, DB, network and SaaS; newly found privileged accounts auto-flagged for onboarding; unmanaged-account inventory trends down.

story: As a platform engineer I want applications to fetch credentials from a broker at runtime so that no privileged A2A secret is hard-coded in application code or config.
acceptance_criteria: In-scope apps retrieve credentials via API/agent at runtime; hard-coded credentials removed; broker access scoped per-application with audit.

story: As a security admin I want phishing-resistant MFA enforced on all privileged access so that stolen passwords alone cannot yield privileged control.
acceptance_criteria: MFA required at the PAM proxy/elevation point for all in-scope privileged access; phishing-resistant factors (FIDO2) for tier-0; exceptions registered with expiry.

story: As an incident responder I want a controlled break-glass path to privileged access so that outages and incidents can be handled without weakening day-to-day controls.
acceptance_criteria: Break-glass accounts sealed, monitored and alert-on-use; checkout requires dual control; every use generates an auto-reviewed incident and post-use rotation.

story: As an endpoint security lead I want local-admin rights removed from users and elevation applied per-application so that malware cannot trivially run with admin rights.
acceptance_criteria: Standing local-admin removed from in-scope endpoints; approved apps elevate per-policy; unauthorized elevation attempts blocked and logged.

story: As a security architect I want privileged entitlements right-sized to actual usage so that accounts hold only the minimum privilege their function requires.
acceptance_criteria: Excess and unused privileged entitlements identified and removed; high-risk combinations flagged; least-privilege baseline reviewed periodically.

story: As a security admin I want vendor and remote privileged access delivered through a controlled, recorded path so that third parties never hold standing or unmanaged privileged access.
acceptance_criteria: Vendor access brokered through the PAM proxy with JIT grants and recording; no standing VPN/admin credentials issued to vendors; per-vendor scope and expiry enforced.

short_title: Cloud entitlement management (CIEM) for privileged cloud identities
story: As a cloud security engineer I want privileged cloud entitlements continuously analyzed so that over-permissioned human and workload cloud identities are detected and remediated.
acceptance_criteria: Privileged and unused cloud entitlements detected across AWS/Azure/GCP; remediation recommendations issued; effective-permission drift monitored.

story: As a platform engineer I want privileged workloads to obtain access via attestation rather than stored secrets so that machine privileged access carries zero standing credentials.
acceptance_criteria: In-scope privileged workloads authenticate via attestation/short-lived tokens; stored standing secrets removed; broker grants scoped and time-bound.

story: As an access governance lead I want periodic attestation of who holds privileged access so that privileged entitlements are re-justified and stale grants are revoked.
acceptance_criteria: All in-scope privileged accounts recertified on a defined cycle; non-attested or orphaned privileged grants revoked; certification evidence retained for audit.

story: As a SOC analyst I want behavioral analytics over privileged sessions and credential use so that anomalous or malicious privileged activity is detected in near real time.
acceptance_criteria: Privileged-session and credential-use telemetry analyzed for anomalies; high-risk events alerted to the SOC; detections mapped to investigation runbooks.

story: As a SOC analyst I want detection of credential-theft techniques against privileged accounts so that pass-the-hash, Kerberoasting and token abuse are caught early.
acceptance_criteria: Detections for pass-the-hash, Kerberoasting, DCSync and token-theft against privileged accounts; alerts correlated to affected accounts; response playbooks triggered.

story: As an operational-resilience lead I want the PAM platform and its emergency-access paths to remain available during outages so that privileged operations and incident response are not blocked by a PAM failure.
acceptance_criteria: PAM platform meets defined availability and recovery targets; break-glass path validated to function during PAM outage; failover and backup of the vault tested periodically.

short_title: Secure admin workstations (SAW/PAW) for tier-0 isolation
story: As a security architect I want all tier-0 and high-impact administration performed from dedicated hardened Secure Admin Workstations isolated from email and web browsing so that credential theft on a standard endpoint can never reach a privileged session.
acceptance_criteria: Tier-0 and in-scope privileged administration performed only from dedicated SAWs/PAWs hardened to a documented baseline (application control, no standing local admin for the operator, patched, monitored); the privileged operating environment is separated from any unprivileged environment and not virtualised inside one; privileged user accounts used from SAWs prevented from accessing internet, email and web services; non-SAW access to tier-0 targets technically blocked at the proxy / conditional-access layer with attempts alerted; SAW fleet inventory and baseline compliance tracked, with exceptions registered with owner and expiry.
